description: compile() of bytes source where the first token is a number immediately followed by invalid-UTF-8 byte triggers an RPython AssertionError -> SIGABRT. Not statically checkable by this toolkit (lives in PEG-parser-generated C, not reviewable RPython source). Recorded for completeness/known-issues tracking only.

file: pypy/module/_struct (exact file TBD -- verify against release branch)
description: struct.unpack("u", ...) reads 4 bytes as a codepoint and passes it to unichr_as_utf8 without validating range (must be <= U+10FFFF, not a surrogate). Leaks as SystemError: unexpected internal exception. CPython removed the legacy 'u' format in 3.9; PyPy still accepts it unguarded.

file: pypy/module/_multibytecodec (exact file TBD -- verify against release branch)
description: codecs.getincrementalencoder(<multibyte codec>)().setstate(<negative int>) hands the state straight to rbigint.tobytes() without checking its signedness precondition. Leaks as SystemError. Affects all 12 multibyte encoders + their StreamWriter; decoders (tuple state) are unaffected. rbigint.tobytes is correctly guarded elsewhere (int.to_bytes raises OverflowError properly) -- setstate looks like the one unvalidated caller.

file: lib_pypy/_lzma.py (not present in main HEAD as cloned -- checkout/branch mismatch, see design doc note)
description: Two defects: (a) line ~562 assigns self._input_buffer = ffi.NONE after freeing it -- ffi.NONE does not exist (should be ffi.NULL per the very next line's check), so the assignment raises AttributeError, leaving a stale freed pointer. (b) line ~575's clear_input_buffer does an unlocked check-then-free of the same field that decompress() correctly locks elsewhere on the same class. Either defect alone or combined produces a double free / SIGABRT, reproduced deterministically and under threading.

file: pypy/module/_io/interp_textio.py (W_TextIOWrapper._dealloc_warn_w -- exact state TBD, see design doc note on version mismatch)
description: TextIOWrapper.detach() followed by ._dealloc_warn(None) segfaults. pypy#5123's fix (7bc330cce0f) added a w_raw-is-None guard to the analogous method in interp_bufferedio.py (the buffered layer) but never touched interp_textio.py's w_buffer field (the text layer) -- an incomplete fix applied to only one layer of the wrapper stack. Every other method on a detached TextIOWrapper raises ValueError cleanly; only this one is unguarded.

TextIOWrapper.detach() then ._dealloc_warn(None) -> SIGSEGV. Bare space.call_method(self.w_buffer, '_dealloc_warn', w_source) with no guard; detach_w:1185 sets w_buffer=None. 17 sibling methods call self._check_attached(space); the buffered-layer twin at interp_bufferedio.py:396 guards with 'if self.w_raw:'. Same defect as PYPY-FUZZ-005, confirmed still unfixed at py3.11 fe2af5843a. Reproduced: exit 139. CPython raises AttributeError (it does not expose _dealloc_warn on TextIOWrapper at all), so PyPy-only.
confirmed_by: pypy-review-toolkit sibling-guard + cross-class scanners; reproduced on PyPy 7.3.23 (194f9f44b505)

description: Second, independent null path into the same site: TextIOWrapper.__new__(TextIOWrapper) then ._dealloc_warn(None) -> SIGSEGV. The interp-level __init__ never assigns w_buffer, so the field is null without any detach() call. Predicted statically during triage, then reproduced: exit 139. Not covered by the PYPY-FUZZ-005 report, which only exercises the detach path.
confirmed_by: pypy-review-toolkit guard triage (static prediction); reproduced on PyPy 7.3.23 (194f9f44b505)

description: The only app-exposed W_TextIOWrapper method with no _check_attached call. Protected only by accident via space.call_method(self, 'flush') at :723 -- an app-level dispatch a subclass can override, after which execution reaches _set_encoder_decoder with w_buffer None. Repro: class T(io.TextIOWrapper) overriding flush to pass; T(io.BytesIO(b''), encoding='utf-8'); t.detach(); t.reconfigure(encoding='latin-1') -> SIGSEGV. SHARED WITH CPYTHON: 3.14.4 also exits 139, and _io_TextIOWrapper_reconfigure_impl has lacked CHECK_ATTACHED since v3.7.0. Report upstream too.
confirmed_by: pypy-review-toolkit sibling-guard scanner; reproduced on PyPy 7.3.23 and CPython 3.14.4

description: format(0xD800,'c') and f'{0xD800:c}' -> SystemError: unexpected internal exception. The guard at :842 checks 0 <= value <= 0x10FFFF, discharging only the range half of unichr_as_utf8's two-clause precondition; the surrogate half needs allow_surrogates=True, which is not passed. All 2048 codepoints in range(0xD800,0xE000) affected. PyPy's own chr() (__builtin__/operation.py:33) and %c (formatting.py:351,:516) both pass allow_surrogates=True behind the same range check, so this is an internal inconsistency. CPython 3.14.4 returns the surrogate string. Fix: add allow_surrogates=True.

csv.reader(iter([]), delimiter='\\ud800').dialect.delimiter -> SystemError: unexpected internal exception. Same two-clause shape as PYPY-REV-004: _get_codepoint (:59-75) performs no surrogate rejection before the value reaches rutf8.unichr_as_utf8. Three sibling sites at :169/:175/:181 plus interp_reader.py:184 share the shape. CPython 3.14.4 accepts the surrogate delimiter and returns it.

BytesIO.close() succeeds silently while a getbuffer() export is live; CPython's _io_BytesIO_close_impl calls CHECK_EXPORTS and raises BufferError. Reproduced: PyPy exits 0 having closed the object, CPython 3.14.4 raises 'BufferError: Existing exports of data: object cannot be re-sized'. A silent divergence rather than a crash, so CONSIDER rather than FIX, but it lets a buffer outlive the object it views.
confirmed_by: pypy-review-toolkit guard triage; reproduced on PyPy 7.3.23 (194f9f44b505)

description: A negative length reaches rbigint.tobytes with no non-negativity check: (0).to_bytes(-1) returns b'' and (1).to_bytes(-1) raises OverflowError('int too big to convert'), where CPython raises ValueError('length argument must be non-negative') for both. Two different wrong behaviours from one missing precondition; the b'' case is the more serious, since a negative length silently produces a value. Not the SystemError shape, so CONSIDER.

A family distinct from PYPY-REV-003: these methods DO call _check_attached at entry, then dispatch space.call_method(self, 'flush'), then dereference self.w_buffer. A subclass whose flush() calls self.detach() nulls the field between the check and the use. Reproduced on PyPy 7.3.23: truncate(), tell(), seek(0) and close() all exit 139. SHARED WITH CPYTHON, which additionally crashes on write() and read(); CPython main is immunized by db4b1948bc4 (gh-143008) but 3.13/3.14 are not, and PyPy has ported neither that nor gh-142594. Sites: :827 :838 :1141 :1244 :1321 plus _read_chunk:894 and _set_encoder_decoder:651.
confirmed_by: pypy-review-toolkit git-history-analyzer; reproduced on PyPy 7.3.23 and CPython 3.14.4
